rules.title: Poor habitat
rules.when: mean of the visual habitat scores <= 5 (of 10)
rules.why: Degraded banks, channel and riparian strip reduce the stream's ability to clean itself and to host life.
rules.advice: Share with the city's river restoration team; repeat the visual check each season.

rules.title: Nutrient enrichment (screening)
rules.when: nitrate >= 25 mg/L as NO3 (a conservative screening value, half the French good/moderate boundary of 50) or orthophosphate >= 0.5 mg/L as PO4 (the French good/moderate boundary); one sample is a screening signal, not a status class
rules.why: Extra nutrients can feed algae; in most fresh waters phosphate is the limiting nutrient, so high phosphate matters most for blooms, while high nitrate mainly signals run-off.
rules.advice: Look upstream for run-off sources (fields, allotments, outfalls) and keep monitoring.

rules.title: Possible cyanobacterial bloom
rules.when: surface = algal-scum, or water-colour = green with water >= 20 C; not counted if the jar/stick test points to ordinary green or filamentous algae
rules.why: Scums in warm water are typical of cyanobacterial blooms, which can poison dogs, livestock and people. Only a lab test can confirm toxins. If the jar/stick test was not done, the scum is treated as a possible bloom (precaution).
rules.advice: Keep dogs and children out of the water and report the bloom to the local authority for testing.

rules.title: Sewage signal
rules.why: Sewage smell or grey water suggests faecal contamination, a route for gut infections in people and animals.
rules.advice: Avoid touching the water, wash hands, and report it to the water utility or municipality.

rules.title: Dead fish
rules.why: Fish kills point to low oxygen, toxins or pollution - an early warning for other animals.
rules.advice: Do not touch the fish; note how many and report to the environment authority.

rules.title: People in contact with affected water
rules.when: people-contact = yes while R3 or R4 fired at the site
rules.why: Exposure turns a water problem into a human-health problem.
rules.advice: Discourage paddling and swimming here until the signal has been checked.

rules.title: Pets or livestock in contact with affected water
rules.when: animal-contact = yes while R3, R4 or R5 fired at the site
rules.why: Dogs and livestock drink and swim in affected water and are often the first victims of blooms.
rules.advice: Keep pets and livestock out of the water and away from scum on the shore.

rules.title: Oil or chemical signal
rules.why: Hydrocarbons and chemicals harm aquatic life and can irritate skin on contact.
rules.advice: Avoid skin contact and report the sheen or smell to the environment authority.

rules.title: Nitrate above 50 mg/L (EU Nitrates Directive level)
rules.when: nitrate >= 50 mg/L as NO3: the level at which the EU Nitrates Directive (91/676/EEC, Annex I) treats surface fresh water as affected by pollution; it is also the EU drinking-water parametric value
rules.why: Stream water is not drinking water, but this level signals run-off that may reach wells and supplies.
rules.advice: Mention it to the water utility; private well owners nearby may want a lab test.

rules.title: No mayfly, stonefly or caddisfly larvae found
rules.when: sensitive-invertebrates = 0 after >= 1 minute of kick-net sampling in a flowing reach
rules.why: Most families of these groups need clean, oxygen-rich water, so finding none suggests poorer conditions over weeks. Some families tolerate pollution, so this is a coarse screen, not a biotic index.
rules.advice: Repeat the sample in a riffle; if still none, share with the ecology team for a full index.
